I am 55 this year, and I have farmed in Quzhou for 40 years. I only finished middle school, so I do not sit and calculate like a scientist, but I do look at the field, remember what happened before, and listen to what other farmers and the extension people say. My land is not small, 129 mu, but my household only has 2 people and some labor goes off-farm, so I cannot make things too complicated. Because of that, I will keep the main land in the usual wheat-maize rotation, and I will leave some land for cotton and millet so I am not putting everything into one crop. If wheat or maize price is bad, at least cotton or millet can help. I have well water, so I am not as afraid of spring drought, but pumping costs money, so I will not irrigate unless the crop stage really needs it.

For the wheat-maize land, I will stay fairly stable this year. Wheat still feeds the household and brings steady money, and maize after wheat is the normal way here. I will not cut fertilizer too hard, because if wheat turns yellow in spring or maize is weak after emergence, then I lose more in yield than I save in cash. But I also will not push too much, because fertilizer, irrigation, and labor all cost money. Cotton I will keep on a smaller block because it takes more management and picking, and with only 2 people at home I cannot expand it too much. Millet I keep because it is simpler, needs less water, and gives me one more way to spread risk if the season turns dry.
